standard_prerequisites.name: Hom(M[2], K') vanishes because M[2] has cohomology only in degrees <= -2 while K' has cohomology only in degrees -1 and 0
standard_prerequisites.use: Kills the factorization target, forcing f = 0 on K'.

core_obligations: Set M = Ker(H^{-1}(alpha)); alpha extends to the distinguished triangle M[1] -> K -> K' -> M[2] (proof lines 22588-22591). The composite K -> K' -f-> K' is zero since f is zero on K, so f on K' factors through the cone as a map M[2] -> K' (proof lines 22592-22594). But K' has cohomology concentrated in degrees -1, 0 while M[2] has cohomology only in degrees <= -2, so Hom(M[2], K') = 0 by the negative-exts lemma of the derived categories chapter, whence f = 0 on K' (proof lines 22594-22596).
proof_roadmap: Build the distinguished triangle from the kernel of H^{-1}(alpha) (proof lines 22588-22591).
Factor f through M[2] and kill it by the vanishing of Hom (proof lines 22592-22596).
